q: The min-entropy H_∞(X) = −log max_x P(X=x) is relevant in cryptography because:
opts: It equals the Shannon entropy for uniform distributions
It is an upper bound on the probability that an adversary correctly guesses X in one try
A distribution with high H_∞ is hard to predict: the best single-guess success probability is 2^{−H_∞}
exp: All are correct: H_∞ = H_1 (Shannon entropy at uniform), and the optimal one-guess success probability is max P(X=x) = 2^{−H_∞}, so high min-entropy ↔ low guessing probability. Min-entropy is the right notion of randomness for cryptography.
